title: perf-bench-scratch-sam-park-2026-03-12
summary: Scratchpad for short latency/throughput runs on Llama-2-13B variants — looking at batching + KV cache tradeoffs. Quick raw numbers, commands, and next steps.
content:
Goal: quick experiments to sanity-check p50/p95 latency and sustained throughput for Llama-2-13B fp16 vs qs8 quantized variant. Focus: small seq lengths (16/64) and production-like concurrent clients (16/64). Also validate KV-cache speedup for chat-like workloads.

Setup:
- Machine: dedicated test node (g5.12x large equivalent) — 8x A10G (simulated local cluster).
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (PR 412 applied: improved continuous batching logic).
- Model builds: llama-2-13b-fp16 (base), llama-2-13b-qs8 (quantized, ~4-bit storage), sequence length caps set per run.
- Docker image: redwood/inference:test-2026-03-10
- Load generator: locust + custom client (scripts in repo under tools/perf/gen_clients).
- Measurement: p50/p90/p95 latency end-to-end (request->first-token), and steady-state throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec). Warmup 60s, measure 180s.

Commands used (approx):
- start server: ./bin/runtime --model /mnt/models/llama-2-13b-fp16 --batching-config configs/batching.yml --kv-cache=true
- load test: python tools/perf/run_load.py --clients 64 --qps 200 --seq 16 --duration 240 --prompt-batch-size 1

Raw notes / quick table (runs timestamped) — these are rough logs, not final telemetry export:

Run A: fp16, seq=16, clients=16, batching=auto, kv-cache=off
- p50: 72 ms
- p90: 130 ms
- p95: 210 ms
- qps sustained: 230 req/s (~3.6k tokens/s)
- notes: stable, batching reduced some variance.

Run B: fp16, seq=16, clients=16, batching=auto, kv-cache=on
- p50: 38 ms
- p90: 68 ms
- p95: 95 ms
- qps sustained: 410 req/s (~6.6k tokens/s)
- notes: KV cache halves latency for short-turn chat flows as expected. Memory remained stable.

Run C: qs8, seq=16, clients=16, batching=auto, kv-cache=on
- p50: 45 ms
- p90: 80 ms
- p95: 120 ms
- qps sustained: 360 req/s (~5.8k tokens/s)
- notes: quantization overhead slightly increases p50 vs fp16+KV but lower memory footprint; throughput still good.

Run D: fp16, seq=64, clients=64, batching=auto, kv-cache=on
- p50: 220 ms
- p90: 420 ms
- p95: 620 ms
- qps sustained: 180 req/s (~11k tokens/s)
- notes: bigger seq length increases tail latency; batching helps throughput but hurts tail for some requests.

Run E: fp16, seq=64, clients=64, batching=max-batch-128, kv-cache=on
- p50: 190 ms
- p90: 380 ms
- p95: 580 ms
- qps sustained: 210 req/s (~12.6k tokens/s)
- notes: forcing larger batches increased tokens/sec at cost of higher p95 spikes occasionally.

Quick conclusions / heuristics so far:
- KV cache is huge for chat-like short-turn latency: ~1.8-2x improvement p50 and ~2-3x on tails in these runs. Good candidate for enabling by default for hosted chat endpoints.
- Quantized (qs8) gives good memory win and modest latency regression vs fp16. Consider qs8 for dedicated/density-focused offering.
- Batching config matters: auto batching gives stable p50 but can create p95 spikes under high concurrency; keeping a max-batch cap (e.g., 64–128) is a useful knob.
- For seq=64 workloads, prefer throughput-optimized routes with bigger batch caps and different SLOs. Might route interactive chat to lower-batch policy to keep tails tight.

Observations / weirdness to follow up:
- Observed occasional p99 > 1.5s in Run D — need to correlate with GC/host/network noise. Add system-level tracing (node-exporter + perf) next run.
- One run showed memory climb over 20 minutes on qs8 variant (maybe allocator fragmentation). Ask Ethan to check our allocator flags.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run with telemetry ON (trace ids attached) to correlate p99 spikes with OS metrics (cpu steal/PCIe stalls). Add perf counters.
- Add controlled single-client sequential requests to isolate KV cache path (no batching).
- Try qs4 (if available) to measure additional CPU overhead vs memory savings.
- Draft short doc for product: "KV-cache default recommendations for chat endpoints" with these numbers + screenshots.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Attach raw CSVs from load generator to Drive (see linked_artifacts).
- Ping Maya for longer-run stability test (6 hours).
- Add an internal metric for batch-size distribution per route.

Slack refs / context:
- convo in #perf-bench: https://slack-redwood/workspace/archives/C02PERF123/p1689001234
- PR with batching improvements: GH PR 412 (linked above)

Random scratch ideas:
- Could we experiment with hybrid routing where short chat requests go to a smaller-seq pinned worker with extremely aggressive KV cache pinned in memory?
- Think about default serving profile: interactive-chat vs long-completion vs embedding. Map batching & max-batch caps per profile.

End of scratchpad. Keep as 'working notes' — will formalize after follow-ups and longer stability runs.
